thread.title: Review N13 installed Swift ownership and qualification gaps

items.text:
Act as the review sub-agent for this task.

Read-only independent review for N13 native-language qualification. Parent is implementation agent working in /Users/jagatranvo/.t3/worktrees/stateless/t3-dfe68040; that fresh worktree is being initialized, so use source /Users/jagatranvo/.t3/worktrees/stateless/t3-ea05e2fb at 57cc38b0abb1c8dcb586d80f44455ab23a8f7a19 for baseline reads now. Never edit any tree, run builds/tests, or touch queue state. Inspect docs/native-parity/N13-INTEGRATION-GATES.md, examples/native-model Swift app and scripts/check-native-model-consumers.py plus related oracle. Known V2 installed failure: main-actor top-level provenance referenced by nonisolated produce/transcode; recommend minimal faithful ownership fix without relaxed checking. Review independent bytes, all25pairs, RunConfig, phase/provenance, exact callbacks and actual Recorder/EvidenceRecorder binder coverage for concrete correctness gaps beyond known compile failure. Return actionable findings and exact file locations, or no findings. Do not spawn monitoring agents. A subsequent review round will inspect final diff and receipts.
I’ll review the specified baseline and oracle read-only, focusing on gaps beyond the known actor-isolation failure. I won’t edit files, run builds or tests, or touch the queue.

The baseline is clean at `57cc38b0abb1c8dcb586d80f44455ab23a8f7a19`. The installed scenario uses real Recorder and EvidenceRecorder paths with exact callback assertions. I’m now checking those assertions against the binder and replay callgraphs, and looking for integration gates the scenario leaves uncovered.

I found a concrete coverage gap: TypeScript replay creates the application without a custom decode-limit provider, so its provider count is zero; the documented four-call replay contract is never asserted. I’m also checking whether the failure controls exercise recorder capture, since direct codec rejections do not cover prefix preservation after a capture callback fails.

There is another definite failure in the Swift causal binder test: it compares the recorder’s stamped RunConfig with the original empty-parameter config. Recorder adds engine and monitor parameters, so that equality cannot hold. The expected config should include those stamps; changing recorder behavior would invalidate the installed byte oracle.

Reviewed clean baseline `57cc38b0abb1c8dcb586d80f44455ab23a8f7a19`. Three additional findings:

- **P1 — Swift causal binder test has an impossible config expectation.** [DeriveCodecTests.swift:181](/Users/jagatranvo/.t3/worktrees/stateless/t3-ea05e2fb/swift/Tests/StatelessnessTests/DeriveCodecTests.swift:181) compares the recorded config with the original empty-parameter config. [Recorder.swift:42](/Users/jagatranvo/.t3/worktrees/stateless/t3-ea05e2fb/swift/Sources/Statelessness/Recorder.swift:42) adds engine/monitor parameters, and snapshot adds observed/evicted counts. Assert the complete expected stamped config. This is a deterministic assertion failure inferred from source.

- **P2 — TypeScript replay omits the required provider-count witness.** [consumer.ts:87](/Users/jagatranvo/.t3/worktrees/stateless/t3-ea05e2fb/examples/native-model/typescript/consumer.ts:87) calls `application()` without a provider; line 32 therefore omits the counted callback. Replay records `limits: 0`, and line 88 excludes limits from its assertions, despite the documented four-call contract. Bind a counted provider for application replay and assert exactly four calls; retain a separate omitted-provider control.

- **P2 — Installed capture-failure coverage is missing.** [Integration gate 5](/Users/jagatranvo/.t3/worktrees/stateless/t3-ea05e2fb/docs/native-parity/N13-INTEGRATION-GATES.md:93) requires coherent Recorder/evidence prefixes and diagnostic ownership after an actual capture callback fails. The applications exercise successful capture and direct codec rejection; for example, [Swift’s controls](/Users/jagatranvo/.t3/worktrees/stateless/t3-ea05e2fb/examples/native-model/swift/Sources/ModelConsumer/main.swift:57) never fail inside a recorder. Add isolated controls that retain one successful turn, fail the bound Output encoder during the next capture, and assert retained steps, phase journal, error ownership, and exact callback counts for both recorder types.

For the known Swift compilation blocker, the smallest faithful fix is `@MainActor` on [produce()](/Users/jagatranvo/.t3/worktrees/stateless/t3-ea05e2fb/examples/native-model/swift/Sources/ModelConsumer/main.swift:91) and [transcode(_:)](/Users/jagatranvo/.t3/worktrees/stateless/t3-ea05e2fb/examples/native-model/swift/Sources/ModelConsumer/main.swift:116), matching their synchronous top-level caller and provenance ownership.

I found no additional byte-oracle or 25-pair enumeration defect in my inspection. No files changed, builds/tests executed, or queue state touched. Final-source execution remains required.

The completed cross-check adds one finding:

- **P2 — Receipts omit executable identity.** [check-native-model-consumers.py:69](/Users/jagatranvo/.t3/worktrees/stateless/t3-ea05e2fb/scripts/check-native-model-consumers.py:69) retains staged source hashes and runner paths, but no hashes for the executed Go, Swift, or Rust binaries. They reside outside the output directory hashed by `save()`. Record each executable’s SHA-256 and size before execution and verify afterward; the Rust engine build stamp does not identify the application binary.

It also confirms that the **TypeScript provider-count discrepancy can pass qualification**: [driver line 71](/Users/jagatranvo/.t3/worktrees/stateless/t3-ea05e2fb/scripts/check-native-model-consumers.py:71) accepts receipts without checking the oracle’s count dictionaries. Alongside supplying TypeScript’s counted provider, normalize and validate capture/replay counters, rejecting missing fields.

The independent review found no defect in the v1/v2 byte construction or all-25-pair enumeration. These remain static findings against `57cc38b0abb1c8dcb586d80f44455ab23a8f7a19`; no execution or queue actions occurred.
